page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is a local-storage and memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed under the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is allocated 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and supports vector and cryptography instructions including AVX-512F and AES-NI. System memory totals 32.0 GB RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is 959 GB of dedicated local SSD storage, accompanied by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate lower-tier computational and memory throughput compared across broader cloud instance baselines. In CPU stress testing, the instance scored 1101.89 on single-core and 2923.84 on multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 941.0 and multi-core score of 2049.0. Memory bandwidth for large 256 MB uncached transfers achieved 20.18 GB/sec read and 18.64 GB/sec write. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server reached 2.97 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and sustained 2.52 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark testing produced a CPU score of 3616.16 and a database operations score of 1081.7.

The primary operational trade-off of this configuration is modest compute capability balanced against high memory density and integrated local SSD space. Rather than raw compute power, cost efficiency stems from bundling 959 GB of fast local SSD storage alongside 32 GB of memory on a 4-vCPU footprint. This configuration suits transactional caching, intermediate data manipulation, NoSQL nodes, staging databases, and operational data stores requiring dedicated local disk and substantial memory overhead without heavy processing needs.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2ne.xlarge is a memory-oriented, storage-backed instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 32.0 GB of system memory, and a dedicated 959 GB local SSD, the instance delivers an 8 GB per vCPU ratio alongside 2 Gbps baseline networking and zero GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the lower quartiles for raw processing, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 2049.0 and 2.97 million Redis SET operations per second. While computational speed and large-block memory bandwidth are constrained, cost efficiency is realized through the density of integrated local solid-state storage and generous RAM capacity on a small core footprint. These characteristics make it suitable for caching layers, lightweight database hosting, log indexing, and memory-dependent storage workloads.
